code_references.scope: For real a,p, integer multiples of the class of a in AddCircle p have dense range iff a/p is irrational. Not joint torus equidistribution, positive-time avoidance or arbitrary-speed lonely runners.

In the file’s Borel/topological normed-space setting, a function continuous on a compact K in a Hausdorff domain is integrable on K for a measure finite on compact sets. Parameter holomorphy, infinite translate sums, normalized Monte Carlo error and global continuation require separate proofs.

For an actual complex Dirichlet character χ and Re(s)>1, the convergent prime product of (1−χ(p)*p^(−s))⁻¹ equals its Dirichlet L-series. Not an arbitrary exceptional automorphic lift, local reflection law, critical-strip product identity or a spectrum-union theorem.

On one fixed measure space, a.e. strong measurability, a common integrable norm bound and a.e. pointwise convergence yield convergence of Bochner integrals. It constructs none of the rank embeddings, measures or domination needed for G∞, and does not identify a fixed arithmetic source.

For finite index type, complex b with positive real part and coefficients c_i, the product-volume integral of exp(−b*Σv_i²+Σc_i v_i) equals (π/b)^(card/2)*exp(Σc_i²/(4b)). With b=c_i=1 it computes the model integrals after real/complex conversion. No identification with an automorphic residue or boundary cohomology is supplied.

For an element q of a normed division ring with ||q||<1, Σ_{n≥0} q^n=(1−q)⁻¹. Matching a χ(p^k)*p^(−ks) series requires multiplicativity/cpow and index-shift adapters. General Hecke coefficients are not automatically powers of one scalar.

An integer polynomial with nonzero constant term admits specified prime-indexed integer/polynomial exponential approximations at its complex roots with factorial error bounds. This is an analytic auxiliary result, not the full Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem, Baker logarithmic independence, motivic independence or an infinite-sum transcendence theorem.

For a>0, x↦a^x has strict derivative a^x*log(a). The paper-specific exponent composition, constants, sign and normalization must still be instantiated; no critical-point or zero-location theorem is supplied.

The oriented real interval integral of x^r is (b^(r+1)−a^(r+1))/(r+1), assuming r>−1 or r≠−1 with zero outside the unoriented interval. To use it for |t^ρ/ρ|, prove the positive-real norm identity and ρ≠0 and factor out its norm. No logarithmic or arithmetic error estimate follows.
For x>0 and x≠1, x^y=x^z iff y=z. Prime-base reciprocal-power reflection therefore requires equality of the exponents; the scalar specialization is a correction route, not a modular symmetry theorem.

For a self-adjoint element of a complex C*-algebra, every complex spectral point is real. No unbounded operator domain, arithmetic realization, homotopy obstruction or zero-coordinate correspondence is constructed.

For the supplied finite free module hypotheses, the trace of a block-diagonal product map is the sum of its traces. This is ordinary algebraic trace, not an infinite/categorical/derived stack trace. The geometric splitting and trace-class/finite-rank realization are not constructed.
